doc.title: Bill Allred interviewed by Monk Rowe, Orlando, Florida, February 24, 2017

title: Switching from clarinet to trombone because of Tommy Dorsey
summary: He started on clarinet, then traded for a trombone after reading in Photoplay that he shared a birthday with Tommy Dorsey.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: So it was in me and I had a couple of uncles who used to play, one played guitar and one played piano, and they would jam at the house once in a while. And I started out on clarinet, pretty, really bad player.
Did you have a metal one?

Yes. I had a metal one that came apart which a couple of people said boy you should have saved that. But anyway, I took it back to the rental place and got a trombone because I heard that Tommy Dorsey and I shared the same birthday, November 19. The total reason for that. And I saw it in Photoplay magazine.
They had a big thing about Tommy Dorsey, oh my God November 19th. So back goes the clarinet.
I love that because that’s the first I’d heard of people talk about — well why’d you go to that instrument. And well I found it behind the couch or whatever. But that’s a first.
